text.headline: Timeline of Albania
text.text: Major events in the history of Albania.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The earliest known settlements in Albania date back to the Neolithic period, around 4000 BC. Archaeological findings suggest that these early communities engaged in agriculture and animal husbandry.

events.headline: Illyrian Tribes Formation
events.text: By 2000 BC, the Illyrians, a group of tribes, began to emerge in the western Balkans, including present-day Albania. They developed a distinct culture and language.

events.headline: Kingdom of Illyria Established
events.text: The Kingdom of Illyria was established around 358 BC, uniting various Illyrian tribes under a single monarchy. This marked the beginning of a more organized political structure in the region.

events.headline: First Illyrian War
events.text: The First Illyrian War began in 229 BC when the Roman Republic intervened in Illyrian affairs. This conflict marked the start of Roman influence in the region.

events.headline: Illyria Becomes a Roman Province
events.text: After a series of conflicts, Illyria was fully conquered by Rome and became a Roman province in 168 BC. This led to significant Romanization of the local population.

events.headline: Division of the Roman Empire
events.text: In 395 AD, the Roman Empire was divided into Eastern and Western halves. Albania fell under the Eastern Roman Empire, also known as the Byzantine Empire.

events.headline: Formation of the Principality of Albania
events.text: The Principality of Albania was established in the early 11th century, marking the emergence of a distinct Albanian political entity. This period saw the consolidation of local power.

events.headline: Ottoman Conquest Begins
events.text: The Ottoman Empire began its conquest of Albania in 1385, gradually subjugating the region over the next several decades. This marked the start of centuries of Ottoman rule.

events.headline: Skanderbeg's Rebellion
events.text: In 1443, Gjergj Kastrioti, known as Skanderbeg, led a rebellion against the Ottomans. He became a national hero for his efforts to resist Ottoman rule for over two decades.

events.headline: Fall of Albania to the Ottomans
events.text: After Skanderbeg's death, Albania fell completely under Ottoman control in 1479. This initiated a long period of Ottoman dominance that lasted for several centuries.

events.headline: Independence from Ottoman Empire
events.text: Albania declared its independence from the Ottoman Empire on November 28, 1912. This event marked the establishment of Albania as a sovereign state.

events.headline: Recognition of Independence
events.text: The Treaty of London in 1913 recognized Albania's independence but also limited its borders. This led to territorial disputes that would affect the country for years.

events.headline: Establishment of the Kingdom of Albania
events.text: In 1928, Albania was declared a kingdom under King Zog I. This marked a significant shift in the political structure of the country.

events.headline: Italian Invasion
events.text: In April 1939, Italy invaded Albania, leading to its annexation. This event marked the beginning of a tumultuous period under fascist rule.

events.headline: Communist Regime Established
events.text: In November 1944, the communist partisans led by Enver Hoxha took control of Albania, establishing a one-party socialist state. This regime would last for nearly 45 years.

events.headline: Fall of Communism
events.text: In 1991, Albania experienced a peaceful transition from communism to democracy. This marked the end of decades of isolation and repression.

events.headline: First Free Elections
events.text: Albania held its first free elections in March 1992, leading to the establishment of a democratic government. This was a significant step towards political reform.

events.headline: Financial Crisis and Civil Unrest
events.text: In 1997, Albania faced a severe financial crisis that led to widespread civil unrest and the collapse of the government. This period was marked by chaos and instability.

events.headline: NATO Membership
events.text: Albania became a member of NATO in April 2009, marking a significant step in its integration into Euro-Atlantic structures. This was a key goal for the country following the fall of communism.

events.headline: EU Candidate Status
events.text: In June 2014, Albania was granted candidate status for European Union membership. This marked a significant milestone in the country's efforts to join the EU.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic reached Albania in 2020, leading to health and economic challenges. The government implemented various measures to combat the spread of the virus.

events.headline: Earthquake Recovery Efforts
events.text: Albania continued its recovery efforts following the devastating earthquake in November 2019. The government and international partners worked to rebuild affected areas.
